dharana.sanskrit_iast: śaktisaṃgamasaṃkṣubdhaśaktyāveśāvasānikam | yat sukham brahmatattvasya tat sukhaṃ svākyam ucyate ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: The delight that comes at the culmination of union with a partner (śakti), when one is absorbed in her through that excitement, is the delight of brahman; that delight is said to be one's own.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: the absorption is symbolic of absorption in the divine energy; the illustration shows that the highest delight comes when duality disappears. He quotes a verse given by Śivopādhyāya saying that scripture speaks of union only to illustrate union with the divine, and that taking it as an injunction for carnal pleasure is folly; the delight belongs to the Self, not to any outer source. Wallis reads śakti as a consecrated female partner.
dharana.technique_name: The Delight at the Culmination of Union
dharana.instruction: Observe only: read and understand this classical description. It is not practised in class.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 69 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the delight that belongs to neither, one's own
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The classical map is two becoming one, and the delight that arises when duality falls away. Recorded as text only.
geometry.svg_hint: two faint circles merging into one, drawn faint to signal observe-only
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Duality dissolving (described)
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the delight that arises when two are no longer felt as two. A picture to understand, not an exercise. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Understanding the verse: the highest delight comes when duality falls away, and it is one's own

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: The delight that comes at the culmination of union with a partner (śakti), when one is absorbed in her through that excitement, is the delight of brahman; that delight is said to be one's own.
adiyogi.method_summary: Classical description: the delight at the culmination of sexual union, when one is absorbed in the partner, is the delight of brahman and belongs to one's own Self. Singh reads it as an illustration of union with the divine. Observe-only in this school: text to understand, with no practice cues.

honesty.disclosure: Door 046 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 46 (verse 69) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Not led as a practice. The verse concerns sexual experience; this school records it as classical text only and gives no practice cues. Nothing here is an invitation to any sexual activity in a class setting. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
